title: Keep it Simple! A Multiple-Choice Task can Benefit Generative Recommendation
abstract: arXiv:2611.19320v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sequential recommendation has recently witnessed growing interest in generative retrieval. One of the most popular approaches is to autoregressively generate the semantic identifiers (SIDs) of items as recommendations. Existing efforts mainly rely on semantic alignment, sophisticated architectural designs, and extensive hyperparameter tuning. However, the conventional learning framework for generative models could have foundational limitations. Specifically, most generative models directly predict target items without explicitly learning negative compositions and relative ranking signals. This is not well aligned with the philosophy of Bayesian personalized ranking (BPR), which emphasizes the importance of relative rankings between positive and negative samples. tldr: 该论文提出只需在生成式推荐的学习目标中加入一个简单的多项选择题辅助任务，即可显式引入负样本和与BPR理念一致的相对排序信号，从而在不依赖复杂架构和大量调参的情况下有效提升推荐效果。
en_tdlr: Adding a simple multiple-choice auxiliary task to the learning objective of generative recommendation effectively incorporates negative samples and relative ranking signals aligned with BPR, improving performance without complex architectures or extensive tuning.
